name: flatcall-inlined
axis: the CONTROL for flatcall — identical loop with the leaf function's body written out at the call site
notes: Same N, same arithmetic, same output as bench/recursion/flatcall; the only difference is that `step` is not a function. Scale-verified. Interleaved min-of-3 on core 6: rust 1.967s, deno 2.453s, vl 2.913s, python(12M) 1.331s. Subtracting this from flatcall gives a per-call cost of ~0 for rust, deno and VL, and ~44ns for CPython. Disassembling VL's module shows a textbook loop: two i32 locals, `block { loop { br_if; i32.xor/mul/add/and; br } }`, no allocation and no bounds checks — VL's emit is optimal here, and the 1.48x-vs-rust / 1.19x-vs-deno gap is the wasm engine (Cranelift) losing to LLVM and TurboFan on a scalar integer dependency chain, not a VL codegen defect.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes
